6bf3c638d3aa2c44fbd458ed1854c4690271371a.summary: Recorded Future's Insikt Group reports on OilAlpha, a campaign it links to threat actors that likely support a pro-Houthi movement. Since May 2022 it has targeted non-governmental, media, humanitarian and development entities, mostly Arabic-speaking Android users, using spoofed Android apps and social engineering over encrypted messengers. The report names SpyNote, SpyMax and njRAT tools. Most attributions are hedged.

hedges: we are linking to threat actors that likely support a pro-Houthi movement agenda.
The group is highly likely to have targeted entities associated with the non-governmental, media, international humanitarian, and development sectors.
The group's operations have reportedly included targeting persons attending Saudi Arabian government-led negotiations.
As of this writing, we suspect that the attackers targeted individuals the Houthis wanted direct access to.
Per victimology assessment, it appears a majority of the targeted entities were Arabic-language speakers and operated Android devices.
OilAlpha threat actors are highly likely to be involved in espionage activity.
It is likely that OilAlpha has used other malware for testing or attack operations.
Barring the discovery of new information or broader geostrategic shifts, OilAlpha is likely to continue using malicious Android-based applications.
